target_customer: E-commerce, SaaS and financial institution merchants that take card payments
problem: Merchants lose revenue to false declines and fraud and have little visibility into dispute and fraud metrics.
business_model: B2B SaaS and rules/model tooling plugged into payment providers (Stripe, Adyen, Checkout, Shopify)
product_category: Payments analytics, fraud detection and approval optimization

founders.name: Saif Farooqui
founders.background_notes: YC page: data scientist at Stripe, Google and Facebook, earlier a healthcare economist. Sole founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Fraud and approval models need payments data and tuning per merchant, plus integrations with several processors; standard ML rather than research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Models trained on merchant payment data improve with use, but Stripe Radar and enterprise vendors have far more data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established fraud vendors already existed; search results about them are 2026 vendor pages, and none shows an action against Corgi Labs.

market_need_then: False declines and chargebacks are a known merchant cost; no dated 2023 spend or demand source was gathered.

branding.domain_note: Earlier name CorgiAI per CB Insights (corgiai.net); current site corgilabs.ai. No purchase history found.

identity.logo: Blue wordmark with a corgi mascot per the company site
identity.visual_style: Blue wordmark, trust badges (SOC 2, PCI DSS, GDPR, ISO 27001)
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and results focused, with a free diagnostic as the main call to action.

rebrands.why: Not stated; CB Insights notes the former name only.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly mascot stands out in fraud tooling, but an unrelated, much larger AI insurer named Corgi (which raised $108M and bought Corgi.com in 2026) now dominates searches for the name.

outcome_analysis: Corgi Labs is active with a team of 3 on the YC page and the company site claims recovered false declines and fraud prevented, without naming customers. Aggregators show conflicting funding (a $3.58M seed II in May 2025 on CB Insights only), so traction and funding cannot be verified. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found.
notes: Unverified aggregator funding: CB Insights lists a $3.58M Seed II (2025-05-09, Epic Angels) and $4.26M total across three rounds; FundedIQ lists a $500K pre-seed from April 2023. Neither confirmed by a second source, so no rounds recorded. The company site logos list Haven Ventures and Capital X without saying they are investors. HQ conflicts across sources (Singapore on YC, Beaverton Oregon on CB Insights). Competitors left empty: only 2026 vendor pages found. Founder education not found.
